note: FR-FACT-3's rise and set reference, fetched 2026-11-04 (V214-19, V214-23; Jupiter and the Moon re-fetched in R183, D-1111). Geometric horizon crossings (no refraction, no dip, the body's centre at 0°) over Bariloche at ground level on the night of 2026-01-15 (ART, UTC-3), to the minute. JPL Horizons has no stars, so Sirius comes from the US Naval Observatory's celestial-navigation API: its computed altitude `hc` (apparent place, before refraction) sampled each minute, the API drops a star below about 1°, so the crossing is a straight-line fit over the ten minutes nearest the horizon (0.18° a minute, linear to 0.001°). Jupiter and the Moon are Horizons' topocentric elevation (`QUANTITIES=4`, `APPARENT=AIRLESS`, site elevation 0) sampled each minute, the crossing interpolated between the two minutes either side of 0°; Horizons' own `R_T_S_ONLY` was not used, since with `TVH` it reports the refracted upper limb over the site's dip. Never edit by hand.
